model: Aidoo Pro BACnet (Wi-Fi + BACnet MS/TP AC interface)
equipment_type: Split / ducted AC unit interface (BACnet MS/TP)
applies_to: Airzone Aidoo Pro interfaces that connect one air-conditioning indoor unit (or Airzone zone system) to Wi-Fi and to a BACnet MS/TP BMS.
summary: Aidoo Pro plugs into an air-conditioning indoor unit and offers cloud control plus a BACnet MS/TP slave port. The integration manual lists 11 objects: on/off, setpoint, room temperature, mode, fan speed, louvre position, communication and error flags, a digital input, auxiliary heat status and an error-code string.
notes: Object names are the Description column of the list of objects; the table gives object type, instance (registration), R/W and values.

Mode values differ inside the manual: the object table gives 1 Auto, 2 Cooling, 3 Heating, 4 Ventilation, 5 Dry, while the detailed description gives 0 Stop, 2 Cooling, 3 Heating, 4 Dry, 6 Ventilation. The table values are shown; check by reading the state text.
BO 0 Auxiliary heat is listed as read-only. An object is only valid while its Out_Of_Service is FALSE; availability depends on the connected unit.
Setpoint and room temperature units are not printed in the manual.
Copy hosted on a retailer manual site (Total Home Supply); no Airzone-hosted copy was found.

integration.summary: In the Airzone Cloud app (Airtools, Bluetooth advanced setup, Integration) set the output to BACnet MS/TP and give the slave address, then wire the RS-485 bus. Write on/off, mode, setpoint and fan speed and read room temperature and the error flags.
setup: The MS/TP slave address is set in the Airzone Cloud app (Airtools > Integration).
RS-485 port 300-115200 bps, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no flow control.
gotchas: Values are only valid while Out_Of_Service is FALSE.
The two mode tables in the manual disagree; confirm the codes on site.

note: Provided as-is. Point availability varies by firmware and options; verify against the live device.
